thread:
natalie: quick FYI from the phoenix-lite int4 onboarding canary — ~0.7% of funcall outputs show array truncation or stray control bytes after the list. only reproducible when batch_size > 1 and stream=true.

diego: ouch. any raw samples?

natalie: yes, pasted one of the failing responses (redacted):
```
{"tool": "list_files", "files": ["a.txt", "b.txt", "c.txt",
```
followed by raw trailer bytes (hex): `7b 22 74 6f 6f 6c 22 3a 20 5b 22 61 2e 74 78 74 22 2c 20 22 62 2e 74 78 74 22 2c 20 22 63 2e 74 78 74 22 2c 02`

sam: sync (no streaming) ok? batch_size=1?

natalie: sync and batch_size=1 are clean. only seen on streaming with batches >1.

diego: sounds like stream merge boundary writing into the same output buffer and a write-length miscalc leaves a trailing control byte or cuts off the closing bracket. could be a token->byte count mismatch in the quant decode path.

sam: repro steps you used?

natalie: ./canary_runner --model phoenix-lite:int4 --profile int4-stream --batching max=8 --streaming --samples 5000 --seed 7

diego: quick mitigation ideas: 1) postprocess enforce-json-balance: on stream flush, run a lightweight parser that checks bracket/brace counters; if counters indicate a single missing ']' or '}' append them and emit a "stream-fixup" metric. 2) short-term: disable streaming for int4 canary or set batching.max=1.

sam: agree. also add an assert in the runtime that output_buffer_pos is reset between sequences. instrument per-request raw-byte dumps (obfuscated) for canary failures.

natalie: tried float16 baseline: 0 failures in 3000 samples. int4 shows ~0.72% (36/5000). filing issue and will PR a postprocess guard that attempts safe-closing of single missing closers and increments a metric. will also gate the fix to canary/dedicated first.

diego: long-term we should audit the quant decode kernel and the streaming boundary logic. if the postprocess fix reduces the noisy incidents, it's likely kernel/flush related.

infra-bot: Canary job phoenix-lite-int4-stream started (id: canary-80102) — logs: https://ci.redwood.example/canary-80102

sam: please tag me and diego on the PR. scheduling a kernel review for next week. :thumbsup:
